messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] gfortran and macos 27
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erich, long time no see.

This is Apple playing numbers games with their versions combined with gfortran thinking it can get the OS version by subtracting 9 from the kernel version.

In short: To set gfortran back on tracks, add the following to your configuration (using config.site <http://config.site/>, or whichever mechanism you prefer):

FFLAGS=-mmacosx-version-min=26.0

(AFAIR 27.0 also works.)

Also notice that Simon is pushing the development version towards using flang instead of gfortran. See his note from 2026-09-21 on this list.

Best,
Peter

messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] gfortran and macos 27
messages.body_plain:
Pronblem solved.
I had gcc from homebrew also installed.
Putting

# GNU Fortran for Apple Silicon:
# Work around the toolchain's invalid default macOS 18.0 target.
FC      = /opt/gfortran/bin/gfortran -arch arm64
F77     = /opt/gfortran/bin/gfortran -arch arm64
FFLAGS  += -mmacosx-version-min=15.0
FCFLAGS += -mmacosx-version-min=15.0

# OpenMP via Homebrew libomp
CPPFLAGS += -I/opt/homebrew/opt/libomp/include -Xpreprocessor -fopenmp
LDFLAGS  += -L/opt/homebrew/opt/libomp/lib -lomp


in ~/.R/Makevars solved the problem.

messages.body_plain:
Erich,

Homebrew compilers are incompatible with Apple's so generally it is not a godd idea to mix them.

There is a much easier solution, simply set

MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=28.0

in your environment (or you can use any other valid macOS version such as 15.0 or 26.0).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] R Commander crashes with X_OpenFont error on Apple Silicon Mac
messages.subject_clean: R Commander crashes with X_OpenFont error on Apple Silicon Mac
messages.body_plain:
Dear R for macOS Development Team,

I am experiencing a reproducible crash when launching R Commander (Rcmdr) on 
my Apple Silicon Mac. I would appreciate your advice on how to resolve this 
issue.

System information:

Mac: MacBook Air with Apple M4 chip

macOS: Tahoe 26.6.2

R: 4.6.1 (arm64)

R Commander (Rcmdr): 2.15.0

EZR (RcmdrPlugin.EZR): 1.70

Tcl/Tk: 8.6.13, installed through the official R macOS package

XQuartz: 2.8.6

Problem:

When I launch R from Terminal and execute:

library(Rcmdr)

R begins loading the required packages but then terminates with the following 
X11 error:

X Error of failed request: BadValue (integer parameter out of range for 
operation)
  Major opcode of failed request: 45 (X_OpenFont)
  Value in failed request: 0xa00228
  Serial number of failed request: 2199
  Current serial number in output stream: 2200

The Terminal then returns to the shell prompt.

Troubleshooting already performed:

Confirmed that Tcl/Tk is available in R.

Confirmed that a basic Tk window can be created successfully.

Confirmed that the Tk wish8.6 application can display text using standard Tk 
fonts.

Confirmed that XQuartz is installed and can display X11 applications.

Refreshed the font cache and restarted XQuartz.

Tried changing Tk font settings, including Helvetica and Courier.

Tried modifying the X11 font path.

Tested R Commander with alternative R options, without success.

The same X_OpenFont error occurs consistently.

I understand that newer Tcl/Tk releases may include fixes related to X11 font 
errors. However, the Tcl/Tk installation bundled with my R environment is 
version 8.6.13.

Could you please advise:

Is this a known compatibility issue involving R Commander, Tcl/Tk 8.6.13, 
XQuartz, and recent macOS versions?

Is there an officially supported way to update Tcl/Tk without breaking the 
existing R installation?

Is there a recommended workaround for running R Commander and EZR on an Apple 
Silicon Mac?

I would prefer to preserve my existing R and EZR installation if possible.

Thank you very much for your time and assistance.

Best regards

messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] ast2ast: bus error on r-oldrel-macos-x86_64 only, not reproducible
messages.subject_clean: ast2ast: bus error on r-oldrel-macos-x86_64 only, not reproducible
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
the CRAN checks of ast2ast 1.1.1 show a bus error on r-oldrel-macos-x86_64 only. All other flavors are OK, including both arm64 flavors. The crash happens in inst/tinytest/test_range_type.R, inside a function compiled at test time:
  f <- function(n) {
    argtypes(n |> type(int))
    i <- 1L:n
    s <- 0L
    for (r in 1L:3L) {
      for (v in i) s <- s + v
      i <- i + 1L
  ? }
    return(s)
  }
  fcpp <- ast2ast::translate(f)
  fcpp(4L)
  *** caught bus error ***
  address 0x7ff811a46993, cause 'non-existent physical address'

What I tried, without being able to reproduce it:
  - ASan/UBSan (local Ubuntu, R-hub), valgrind, clang + libc++
  - GitHub Actions macos-15-intel (Xcode 16.4, Apple clang 17), R 4.5.3 and R release: the full test suite and R CMD check --as-cran both pass The mac builder only offers R-devel, so I can't test the oldrel x86_64 setup there.

Does anybody have advice on how I could set up a test environment to reproduce the error?It would also be helpful to know which macOS/Xcode version the r-oldrel-macos-x86_64 machine is using.
Thanks a lot and best regards,Konrad Krämer

> On 27/10/2026, at 18:26, Konrad Krämer via R-SIG-Mac <r-sig-mac at r-project.org> wrote:
> 
> Dear all,
> the CRAN checks of ast2ast 1.1.1 show a bus error on r-oldrel-macos-x86_64 only. All other flavors are OK, including both arm64 flavors. The crash happens in inst/tinytest/test_range_type.R, inside a function compiled at test time:
>   f <- function(n) {
>     argtypes(n |> type(int))
>     i <- 1L:n
>     s <- 0L
>     for (r in 1L:3L) {
>       for (v in i) s <- s + v
>       i <- i + 1L
>     }
>     return(s)
>   }
>   fcpp <- ast2ast::translate(f)
>   fcpp(4L)
>   *** caught bus error ***
>   address 0x7ff811a46993, cause 'non-existent physical address'
> 
> What I tried, without being able to reproduce it:
>   - ASan/UBSan (local Ubuntu, R-hub), valgrind, clang + libc++
>   - GitHub Actions macos-15-intel (Xcode 16.4, Apple clang 17), R 4.5.3 and R release: the full test suite and R CMD check --as-cran both pass The mac builder only offers R-devel, so I can't test the oldrel x86_64 setup there.
> 
> Does anybody have advice on how I could set up a test environment to reproduce the error?It would also be helpful to know which macOS/Xcode version the r-oldrel-macos-x86_64 machine is using.
> Thanks a lot and best regards,Konrad Krämer
